problem: Can source-generated reference records distinguish the fixed projective implementation from every canonical implementation with a composition-compatible three-bit sign action, despite unknown axis-dependent readout channels?
obligation: forward realization of reference preparations, then attachment transport and full-record identification
conjecture: The eight actions have unique predictions from matching bypass tables and the 11 basis reference. All are excluded exactly when C_A, C_B, Delta_AZ and Delta_BZ are nonzero. Blind Z channels give genuine record aliases; the missing 11 reference admits nuisance refits even when the actual Z channels are informative.

action_class.group: S4 acting through the actual Boolean source permutations
action_class.placement: flip ideal labels before K and the axis-specific detector record channels; quantum continuations are not relabelled into new states
action_class.axis_rule: the flip bit of each detector is independent of axis, but its stochastic readout channel may depend on axis

channel_class: K tensor R_A,axis tensor R_B,axis, conditionally independent given ideal records, fixed across reference and probe uses of that axis

records.basis_references: no herald requested; keep all nine detector cells

degeneracy_census.blind_column_rule: replace both columns by their arithmetic mean

rivals: informative X probes suffice when a Z response is blind
unknown noise must be numerically fitted or physically admitted before prediction
the 11 reference adds no identifying information
record aliases imply equal postmeasurement continuations
predicted_survivor_rule: (not vA or not AZ) and (vH xor vB or not C_B) and (not vB or not BZ) and (not(vH xor vA) or not C_A)
scope: Exact mathematical comparison for the fixed canonical/projective sources and eight ideal-label actions. No arbitrary correlated, context-dependent, or axis-dependent sign-action model is classified. No physical-admission prerequisite, measured records or finite-sample confidence claim.
